summary: This work demonstrates a monolithic platform combining aluminum superconducting circuits on 4H-SiC with piezoelectric 42% Sc-content AlScN on the same substrate for integrated quantum acoustics, enabled by selective AlScN removal to expose low-loss SiC regions. Al-on-SiC resonators achieve $Q_i = 7.5 	imes 10^4$ (single-photon, $T_1 = 2.9$ μs at 4.175 GHz) while retained AlScN regions support surface acoustic waves with propagation losses of $1.02 	imes 10^{-3}$ dB/μm for Sezawa modes ($	au_{	ext{phonon}} = 7.6$ μs) and $3.16 	imes 10^{-3}$ dB/μm for Rayleigh modes ($	au_{	ext{phonon}} = 3.4$ μs) at 7 mK.
motivation: Hybrid superconducting-phonon quantum systems require scalable platforms combining strong piezoelectric coupling, ultralow acoustic loss, and superconductor compatibility without suspended structures. Existing heterostructures like thin-film LiNbO$_3$ suffer from high cryogenic losses (1–2 μs phonon lifetimes) and integration challenges.
method: Sputter-deposited 1 μm AlScN (42% Sc) on 4H-SiC was selectively etched via TMAH to expose SiC; aluminum CPW resonators were fabricated on exposed regions while retaining AlScN patches for phonons. Superconducting resonator performance was measured via dilution-refrigerator VNA ($<20$ mK); acoustic delay lines ($L_0 = 500$–10,000 μm) were characterized cryogenically using echo-based propagation loss extraction.
result: The platform simultaneously achieves competitive superconducting coherence ($T_1 = 2.9$ μs, $Q_i 	o 7.5 	imes 10^4$) and microsecond-scale phonon lifetimes with measured electromechanical coupling $K^2 = 4.3	ext{%}$ (theoretical max 8%), establishing a scalable monolithic architecture for circuit quantum acoustodynamics and measurement-based quantum computing.
